title: Strict quotient-system finite exceptional mapping adjunction
statement:
theorem integralDualizing_system_finite_adjunction
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (G : CoefPairingSystem l E (finiteDualizingCompactification D X) S)
    (Q : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
    (eQ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedEvaluation l E X n).obj (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≅
        integralDualizingFiniteTerm l E D X n)
    (hQ : ∀ {m n : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m),
      (coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition l E X h).app (coefTraceInput l E X Q) ≫
          (normalizedDVRRes l E X h).map (eQ n).hom =
        (eQ m).hom ≫
          (Adjunction.ofIsRightAdjoint (normalizedDVRRes l E X h)).homEquiv _ _
            (integralDualizingFiniteComparison l E D X hl h)) :
    Nonempty ((sfIntegralConstructible l E X).ι.op ⋙ coefPairingHom l E X S Q ≅
      integralDualizingSupportSystemHom D l E X S G)

proof.text: On simultaneous quotient-system resolutions use the finite exceptional mapping-complex transpose (projection, evaluation and exceptional counit). Finite duality site comparison identifies it with ordinary etale internal exceptional adjunction. This comparison has quotient-system compact support as its target argument, without any integral compact-support limit.

The finite exceptional counit coefficient square and hQ identify each quotient transition with the corresponding transition of this same transpose. Thus the maps are a map of strict system Hom complexes. Naturality of the projection/evaluation word gives naturality in K before localizing; do not lift a family of isomorphisms independently at the finite levels.

Residue Tor invariance puts every reduction of a fixed integral constructible input in the finite-Tor domain. Every evaluated map is transported from the ordinary internal exceptional adjunction and is invertible. Exact tower evaluations detect quasi-isomorphisms, making the already constructed map invertible. This is checked separately for each input; no interval uniform over all inputs is claimed.
